references.text: The same chapter describes how the blood from the guilt offering is applied to the right earlobe, the right thumb, and the right big toe of the person being cleansed, showing a parallel ritual with oil.
An identical ritual for a poor person being cleansed from leprosy, where the oil is applied to the same places over the blood of the guilt offering.
At the consecration of Aaron and his sons, blood was applied to the right earlobe, the right thumb, and the right big toe, the same body parts as in the cleansing ritual.
During the priests' consecration, blood was applied to the right earlobe, the right thumb, and the right big toe, a parallel ritual demonstrating sanctification.
The next verse describes what is done with the remaining oil left on the priest's palm.
